source.provider: Technical University of Munich / Max Planck Institute for Dynamics and Self-Organization
source.title: Data underlying the publication: Network topology enables efficient response to environment in Physarum polycephalum
source.scientificScope: Raw microscopy and code underlying experiments on transport-network topology and environmental response in the acellular slime mold Physarum polycephalum.

provenance.verification: Official university research-data repository record checked before admission to specimen queue.
provenance.identityRule: When a concrete file is selected, record repository filename, repository-provided identity/checksum when available, retrieval date, byte size, and a locally computed content hash before five-organ ingestion.

boundedSamplePolicy.reason: The source archive is approximately 255 GB. ZENOMORPH Level-1 requires a small traceable specimen before any bulk acquisition.
selectionRequirements: select a source file or bounded excerpt that contains actual time-varying network/microscopy information rather than only prose metadata
preserve source filename and experiment context
prefer a specimen that permits extraction of explicit relations or temporal network change
do not pre-label the material as a model for ZENOMORPH
record deterministic extraction or sampling rule

blindIngestionInstruction: Treat this as unfamiliar external material. Inspect and metabolize it under existing organ rules.
forbiddenHints: Do not tell organs that slime-mold transport should be copied into ZENOMORPH.
Do not predeclare that decentralization, adaptation, routing, memory, or self-organization are the lesson.
Do not map Physarum tubes onto named ZENOMORPH organs before metabolism produces such a candidate independently.
organRoute: DROPLET: bind source/version/license and acquire one bounded public specimen
MUTHER: read/decompose/recombine observations without supplied analogy
GUT: classify absorbable structure, uncertainty, waste and candidate metabolic effect
VAJRA: attack anthropomorphic/network analogy, provenance leakage and topology claims unsupported by specimen structure
SHROOMING: expose downstream interpretation only after upstream effects exist

crossFoodRole.urbanCounterexample: A highway/network label without actual relations must remain structurally empty; Physarum material must likewise earn relation claims from observed structure, not biological naming.
crossFoodRole.maleCNSCounterexample: Unlike a connectome, Physarum may express changing transport geometry without neurons; ingestion must not assume that every persistent relation is a synaptic-style edge.

nextGate: Acquire and hash one bounded microscopy/network specimen, then run the existing five-organ path and held-out cross-food regression before any structural candidate can enter isolated morphogenesis.
